Hi Olivia — great to meet you both yesterday. Below is a concise recommended shortlist tuned for FinLytics' priorities, plus the artifacts we attached. I kept notes on expected cost and latency at typical interactive settings (seq len ~512, batch=1).

Recommended shortlist (ordered by tradeoff):

1) RW-Titan-13B-q4_0 (recommended starter)
   - Rationale: Near-LLM quality for extraction tasks with a much lower cost envelope than 70B. Works well with prompt templates for high-precision entity extraction.
   - Typical median user latency: ~120-160ms per response (GPU p99 ~360ms)
   - Cost ballpark: ~$0.60 / 1k input+output tokens (hosted)
   - When to pick: interactive UI, want good quality + low cost; if you can accept occasional edge-case misses.

2) RW-Open-70B-fp16 (recommended for highest quality)
   - Rationale: Best quality for nuanced summaries and hard extraction cases where context and reasoning matter.
   - Typical median latency: ~260-350ms (p99 higher, depends on instance type)
   - Cost ballpark: ~$3.50 / 1k tokens
   - When to pick: batch post-processing for highest recall/precision or when quality degradation is unacceptable.

3) RW-Economy-7B-int8 (recommended for heavy scaling)
   - Rationale: Extremely low cost for bulk processing and for pre-filtering / candidate generation. Not as strong on subtle extraction.
   - Typical median latency: ~70-110ms
   - Cost ballpark: ~$0.18 / 1k tokens
   - When to pick: large-scale reprocessing, pre-filtering for routing to a higher-quality model.

Artifacts attached: finlytics-benchmark-report.pdf (summary of internal evals on finance datasets), prompt_set_v1.csv (example prompts + expected labels). Benchmarks: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/finlytics-2026

Next steps I suggest:
- You run the provided prompt set against the three variants (we can spin up short-lived eval endpoints)
- We supply a small sample of inference credits for the POC and a 6-week pilot template if you want to formalize timing
- Priyom will share a quick runbook for accurate comparison (batching, quant settings, KV cache)

If you’re good with that I’ll request trial credits and share the pilot plan + DocuSign link.

Cheers,

Hi Olivia — quick technical notes to make the eval results reproducible on your side: 

- Use the provided prompt_set_v1.csv as-is for initial comparatives; we strongly recommend including the untruncated inputs for extraction tests.
- For RW-Titan-13B-q4_0: enable max_new_tokens=256, temperature=0.0 for deterministic extraction; set continuous_batching=false for single-request latency parity.
- For RW-Open-70B-fp16: use batch_size=4 when running offline benchmarks to reduce cost; keep streaming=false for stable p99 measurements.
- Metrics to collect: exact-match (entities), F1 (span-level), median latency, p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens.

Notes on quality regressions: if you see a drop in extraction precision vs the benchmark report, please: 
1) send the raw input + Redwood request_id (we’ll correlate with KV-cache hits and recent kernel selections)
2) confirm quantization setting (q4_0 vs int8 can change tokenization edge-cases)

I attached a CSV with a small curated prompt set (prompt_set_v1.csv) — feel free to extend and send back. Happy to run a side-by-side if you share a temporary s3 with anonymized examples.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus / Priyom — this is helpful. We ran a quick pass on 150 docs: 

- RW-Titan-13B-q4_0: good balance, extraction precision 0.91 F1, a few missed company-name edge cases
- RW-Open-70B-fp16: precision 0.96 F1, noticeably better on nested entities; cost is a concern for interactive at scale
- RW-Economy-7B-int8: fast but misses ~12% of extraction labels

We think a hybrid approach makes sense: RW-Titan-13B-q4_0 for majority of real-time UI calls, and batch re-run with RW-Open-70B-fp16 for high-value reports. 

Procurement asks: trial credits, SOC 2 evidence, and a sample pilot agreement with milestones (can you include pricing for the two-tier approach above?). Can you also list what anonymized data you would need for the POC?
